events.name: Storm Lucy — August 11, 2026 Derecho
events.area: Northern Indiana — nearly the entire NIPSCO electric service territory — plus ComEd's south region in northeast Illinois (Chicago south suburbs)
events.customers_affected_note: Official NIPSCO outage summary (updated Aug 13, 2026); media tallies during the event ran as high as ~313,000. Roughly 60% of NIPSCO's electric customer base. Illinois adds ~287,000 ComEd customers from the Aug 11 storms (~410,000 across the Aug 11–12 rounds) — see Illinois impact.
events.peak_gust_reported_note: Localized gusts up to 124 mph reported in media coverage; 99 mph is the highest SPC-logged measured gust in the corridor.
events.deaths_note: At least 2 deaths reported in the broader Aug 10-12 severe weather outbreak (press reports).
events.city_peak_note: Largest city outage counts as of Aug 13, 2026 (press).
events.followup: A second round of storms on Aug 12 produced additional outages and flash flooding in Lake, Porter, Jasper, and Newton counties. Indiana National Guard deployed to assist.
events.infrastructure_damage: Extensive tree damage, blocked roadways, entangled power lines, damaged poles, and significant damage to transmission lines, substations, and distribution facilities (NIPSCO).

sources.label: WNDU: largest outage event in company history
ComEd: 99% restored after Aug 11-12 storms (press release)

illinois_impact.tornado_note: NWS confirmed six tornadoes in the south and southwest suburbs on Aug 11, including an EF-1 that tracked through Homewood, Glenwood, and Thornton.
illinois_impact.restoration_note: ComEd restored ~99% of impacted customers by Aug 15–16 with 4,500+ personnel and mutual-assistance crews — one of its largest restoration efforts of the year.
